title: Complete proof of Erdős Problem #1095: The Erdős-Selfridge Function

problemStatement.plain: Formal investigation in number theory: Complete proof of Erdős Problem #1095: The Erdős-Selfridge Function.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Proved gFunc_exists theorem, eliminating the sole axiom. File now has 0 axioms, 0 sorries. Used Kummer theorem (carry-free base-p arithmetic) with explicit witness n=2P-1 where P is primorial product. Status upgraded from axiomatized to verified.
builtItems: Proved gFunc_exists theorem (was axiom) — 0 axioms now
Defined smoothProd, mod_pred_of_dvd_succ, mod_ge_of_dvd_succ_pow, carry_free_of_mod_ge helper lemmas
insights: Core issue: g(k) definition uses sorry in Nat.find existence proof
Need to show: ∃ n > k+1, all prime factors of C(n,k) > k
Simple witness k!+k+1 does NOT obviously work (C(p,k) can have small factors)
Ecklund-Erdos-Selfridge 1974 proved existence, but the proof is non-trivial
10 axioms: 5 deep bounds (EES, Konyagin, LCM, ELS), 5 concrete values (g(2)=3,...,g(6)=143)
Concrete values g(2)=3, g(3)=7 are verifiable: C(3,2)=3 (only factor 3>2), C(7,3)=35=5*7 (both>3)
The 3 sorries are actually 1 sorry repeated 3 times (same existence proof)
Fix priority: prove existence → this eliminates all 3 sorries at once
CRITICAL BUG FIXED: concrete value axioms were INCONSISTENT with code definition (n > k+1), could prove False
Correct values: g(2)=6, g(3)=7, g(4)=7, g(5)=23 — old axioms g(2)=3, g(4)=23 etc. were wrong
Witness k!+k+1 was wrong: C(29,4) has factor 3<=4
Refactored to axiomatized g: 4 specification axioms replace buggy Nat.find definition
g(5)=23 proved by ruling out n=7..22 via interval_cases + prime factor checks
Existence of g(k) proved via carry-free base-p construction: for each prime p<=k, the witness n=2P-1 has all base-p digits dominating those of k
Key lemma: if p^a|(n+1) with p^a>k, then n%p^i >= k%p^i for all i, giving zero carries by Kummer
Imported KummerTheoremOQ03 for choose_coprime_of_no_carries; no new axioms needed
nextSteps: Prove existence of g(k) constructively to eliminate 4 axioms for g
Check if Mathlib has Lucas/Kummer theorem for binomial coefficients
Compute and prove g(6) from axioms
